headline: M23 has held the Rubaya coltan mines since 30 April 2024
detail: UN investigators say the armed group occupies Rubaya town and the whole surrounding coltan mining area, and controls the routes from there into Rwanda.

headline: At least US$800,000 a month for M23 from one mining area
detail: The UN Group of Experts estimates M23 collected this from taxing coltan production and trade at Rubaya in 2024, with around 150 tonnes a month smuggled across the border into Rwanda.

headline: Rwanda exported about 1,000 t more coltan in 2024 than its geology predicts
detail: Until 2022 Rwanda's coltan exports tracked its tin-ore exports as the region's geology would predict. From 2023, with Rubaya in armed-group hands, they pulled away: an excess of about 760 t in 2023 and 1,040 t in 2024, in line with UN estimates of Rubaya output under M23.
method: Expected coltan = Rwanda's cassiterite exports × 25/75 (regional geology, cited by the UN Group of Experts); excess = reported coltan exports − expected. Comtrade data.

headline: Sanctions have hit the refinery, the army and a bank — not the coltan exporters
detail: Since 2025 the US and EU have sanctioned Rwanda's gold refinery, its army, its defence ministry and a military savings bank. None of the seven Rwandan coltan exporters that Global Witness links to Rubaya has been designated.
method: Comparison of the OFAC and EU designation lists (2025–Oct 2026) against the exporters named by Global Witness (Jun 2026).

headline: Conflict gold still reached Kigali's refinery a year after EU sanctions
detail: The US Treasury says at least 60 kg of gold from M23- and army-held areas of South Kivu moved through Rusizi to Gasabo Gold Refinery in early 2026, about a year after the EU listed the refinery.
